propositions: The Mirror Guard workflow reds on a single diverged Gerrit/GitHub SHA sample despite the module's docstring requiring sustained-divergence absorption at the alarm layer to tolerate expected ~15s post-submit replication lag.

The primary watcher (mirror-guard.yml, single-sample run) lacks the evaluation window that the secondary watcher (CloudWatch, 2x5-min sustained) correctly implements, causing transient lag to trigger false-positive alarms during merge bursts.

The designed lag-absorption capability was never wired into the workflow surface—an incomplete implementation that shipped with commit d96628c9dca as a scope-of-work omission in the introducing change.

An in-process evaluation window in run() and main() with configurable retry/delay (default 3 attempts x 45s, ~90s window) must re-sample on divergence and converge to healthy, while genuine stalled or foreign divergence remains loud and fails.

The fix implements the module's own designed capability portably (lives in the CLI, not CI-provider state) and strictly maintains today's failure semantics: today's failures minus only lag-that-converges-within-window, with GitHub-ahead cases always failing.
